rounds.notes: Independent-grade pass (post-rebase, pre-publication) found: `if (halfWidth <= 0) fallback` does not catch NaN (every ordered comparison with NaN is false), unlike getBodyHalfWidth/getBodyHalfHeight's `if (v > 0) return v` guard, so a malformed NaN half-extent silently poisoned the spatial grid instead of falling back. Fixed by mirroring the helper's `v > 0` accept check exactly; added a regression test (`falls back to radius for a malformed NaN halfWidth/halfHeight instead of inserting NaN`) confirmed to fail against the unfixed code and pass against the fix. RunStats fingerprint re-verified byte-identical after the correction.

independent_grade.notes: The change correctly optimizes the spatial grid insertion hot-path by eagerly extracting component data from the ECS stores to avoid function call overhead. The fallback logic handles the tricky NaN edge case perfectly: by mapping any value where `stored > 0` is false (which includes NaN and negatives) to 0 first, the subsequent `<= 0` fallback trigger evaluates to true. This exactly mimics the early-exit behavior of the `getBodyHalfWidth`/`getBodyHalfHeight` helpers without risking NaN poisoning the grid. The fix is minimal, strictly scoped, and comes with a deterministic regression test that explicitly validates the NaN case.
